subject: Stonebridge inference capacity and SLO alignment — post-call recap
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>
To: Elliot Jacobs <elliot.jacobs@stonebridge.health>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.inference>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 30 Sep 2025 15:10:00 +0000
Subject: Stonebridge inference capacity and SLO alignment — post-call recap

Thanks again for your time today — quick recap and proposed next steps from our side. Short summary of what we captured on the call (please correct anything I missed):

Pain points / goals
- High-throughput document classification and extraction in production (claims triage).
- Tight latency need for interactive triage UI: ~P95 < 120 ms for short responses (~64 tokens).
- Peak traffic spikes (seasonal) with sustained bursts up to ~250 qps for short queries; baseline ~40 qps.
- Data residency & PHI: must run in a VPC private deployment for any PHI-processing pipelines.

Model/workload constraints
- Primary model: fine-tuned decoder-only for extraction + reranking. Candidate size: 7B–13B quantized.
- Typical input lengths: 150–700 tokens (documents vary); many short prompts for triage UI.

Topology preferences discussed
- Prefers Redwood Private (VPC) for PHI workloads; evaluating Dedicated for non-PHI services as cost alternative.
- Important: automated fallback to lower-cost variant if Dedicated capacity constrained; multi-variant routing discussed.

Immediate asks / action items (mine)
1) Send an SLO mapping matrix that aligns your P95/P99 latency targets to estimated GPU and batch sizing — attached template (SLO-template-20250930.xlsx).
2) A rough capacity estimate to cover baseline + 2x seasonal burst (will attach a ballpark CSV).
3) Technical deep-dive note from our infra/ops on KV caching, batching strategy, and VPC packaging by EOD Wed.

Attachments: call-recording-20250930.mp3 (full call), SLO-template-20250930.xlsx

Proposed next steps for Stonebridge
- You confirm peak qps numbers and representative token distribution (sample histogram if available).
- We'll schedule a 45-minute technical session (ops + infra) for Thursday 10/2 to go over topology options and a preliminary capacity estimate.

If that aligns, I’ll loop in Grace (ops) and Jordan (solutions) on the technical session invite.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0189

Subject: Re: Stonebridge inference capacity and SLO alignment — post-call recap

Karthik — thanks for the clear summary. Everything there looks right; a couple clarifications from our side: 

- The 250 qps figure is peak *for a single region* during open-enrollment spikes (roughly 2–3 hours/day for ~2 weeks). Baseline steady-state is closer to ~35–45 qps across the cluster.
- Token distribution: median ~85 tokens, 75th ~240, 95th ~560. I can share anonymized sample histograms (no PHI) by EOD tomorrow.
- PHI handling: any document containing PHI must remain in the VPC-private environment. Non-PHI enrichment can use Dedicated/hosted if the routing preserves isolation.

On timeline: procurement will need an initial SOW + a security checklist before we can spin up a private environment. Procurement contact is procurement@stonebridge.health (copied here).

We can do Thu 10/2 at 15:00 ET for the technical session — please send a calendar invite. Also include any preliminary capacity estimate you have; that will help procurement start the internal approval.

—Elliot

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.inference>
To: Elliot Jacobs <elliot.jacobs@stonebridge.health>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 1 Oct 2025 09:18:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Stonebridge inference capacity and SLO alignment — technical notes ahead of Thu session

Elliot / team — looping in some targeted technical notes so Thursday’s session can focus on tradeoffs and costs. I’ve kept it high-level and flagged assumptions.

Assumptions (please flag if we should change):
- Query mix: 70% short (<= 120 tokens), 20% medium (121–400), 10% long (>400).
- Peak single-region short-query QPS: 250 (burst), baseline short-query QPS: 40.
- Target SLOs: short-path P95 <= 120 ms, short-path P99 <= 220 ms.

Recommendations / topology options
1) VPC Private (recommended for PHI):
   - Topology: 2 availability zones, autoscaling Redwood workers behind a router with KV cache pinned to local worker nodes for hot prefixes.
   - Model: start with a 7B quantized variant for short-path (fast token throughput) + 13B quantized for long-form fallback.
   - Batching: continuous batching with dynamic batch cap (short-path cap = 32 tokens/batch target) to preserve tail latency.
   - GPUs: ballpark for short-path 250 qps bursts — ~6 x A10G equiv for peak headroom (with batching + KV cache). Capacity-estimate-20251001.csv attached with scenarios.

2) Dedicated (reserved) for non-PHI:
   - Can reduce unit costs; recommend separate pool with identical routing policies and automatic fallback to hosted variants if capacity saturates.

Caching / quantization notes
- KV cache: aggressive prefix caching for repeated document kernels will reduce token generation significantly; requires session affinity.
- Quantization: 4-bit dynamic quant recommended for 7B; evaluate accuracy drift on your eval set (we’ll run a quick eval if you provide a dev set).

Operational asks for Thursday
- Elliot: a small anonymized sample of token-length histogram and an example worst-case document (no PHI in shared sample).
- Procurement: can you share the security questionnaire so we can pre-populate answers? (we’ll attach our SOC2 cert and a short network diagram).

Attachments: topology-diagram-20251001.pdf, capacity-estimate-20251001.csv

I’ll bring an ops runbook sketch to the call that maps autoscale thresholds to costs and latency tradeoffs.

—Grace
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Ops | Redwood Inference
